transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I... well, my manager actually suggested I come in. I hope that's okay. I've just been having a little bit of trouble at work lately. I'm a waitress, and usually, I'm really good at my job, I promise. But recently... I guess I've just been a little distracted? 

My manager got a bit worried because... well, I guess I started freezing up sometimes in the middle of a shift. Just for a second! But apparently, I was doing things a bit out of order, too. Like, the other day, I was just standing by the soda station, and I had the cash drawer key in my hand, but I wasn't closing out checks... I was just sort of repeating table numbers to myself. It sounds silly, I know. I really didn't mean to scare anyone or cause a fuss. Does that make sense? I just want to get back to being a good employee.
Did you have similar attention or distractibility problems as a child, before age 12?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I was actually a really good student back then, I promise. I always tried my best to pay attention in class and... well, I never wanted to cause any trouble for my teachers or my parents, you know? 

So, no, I didn't have any issues with being distracted when I was little. I was always very well-behaved and focused on my schoolwork. I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I really didn't have any trouble like this until just recently. Is it okay that I didn't have those problems back then?
Have you had any head injury or other medical problem around the time these symptoms started?

Oh, no... no, nothing like that. I haven't hit my head or been sick or anything. I try to take really good care of myself, you know? I haven't had to go to the doctor for anything else lately, so physically I think I'm doing really well. 

I hope that's helpful? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so I'm not wasting your time. Is it okay that I haven't had any other medical problems?
During those episodes when you freeze up, do you feel aware of what’s happening around you?

Um... I think so? I mean, I don't completely blank out or anything, I promise. It's more like... I'm just sort of caught up in my own head for a second? 

I can still hear the restaurant noises, like the plates clinking and people talking, but it's just... maybe a little fuzzy? Or like I'm just really focused on whatever I'm thinking about. I try really hard not to let it happen, and I usually snap right back to it if someone says my name or bumps into me. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm not trying to be vague, it's just a little hard to explain exactly how it feels. Am I answering that right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have these episodes started after any major stress or upsetting event in your life?

Um... no, I don't think so. There hasn't been any big drama or... or trauma or anything like that. I mean, work gets a little busy at the restaurant sometimes, but it's nothing I can't handle, I promise. I try really hard to keep things peaceful and just, you know, do a good job. 

So there wasn't any huge upsetting event before this started. Things have been pretty normal, honestly. I hope that's okay? I know sometimes there's supposed to be a specific reason for why things like this happen, but I just don't have anything like that to report. Am I still giving you the right kind of answers? I just really want to be helpful.
During these episodes, do you ever lose awareness or black out completely?

No, no, I definitely don't black out. I would tell you if I did, I promise. It's really just... like I said, just getting a little too caught up in my thoughts for a minute. 

I'm always still there, you know? I never completely lose track of where I am or what's going on. I know that would be a lot worse, and I'm really glad it's not like that. I'm still able to do my job and everything, so it's really not that bad. 

Is that what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it clearly so you don't worry that it's something more serious than it is.
During these episodes, do you ever feel like another person or force is taking over your body?

Oh, gosh, no. No, definitely nothing like that. I promise it's just me in here. 

I don't feel like I'm being controlled or possessed or... or whatever that would be. It's really just me getting a little spacey or distracted for a second. I would absolutely tell you if I felt like someone else was taking over, because that sounds really scary, and I'd want you to know. But it's just my own thoughts, I swear. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm making things up or being difficult by saying no to so many things. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's happening. Does that make sense? I'm trying to be a good patient, I really am.
During these episodes, do you ever have gaps in your memory for what happened?

Um, no... no, I remember everything. There aren't any blank spots or... or missing time or anything like that. I promise I'm totally aware of what happened afterward. 

I mean, sometimes I might forget to grab an extra side of ranch for a table if we're super slammed, but just normal forgetting, you know? Not because of these... moments. I always know what went on. 

I really hope it's okay that I keep saying no to all these things. I feel a little bad that I don't have more to give you. Am I still being helpful? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right and giving you what you need.
Have you noticed any change in your memory or thinking outside of these episodes, like forgetting recent events, trouble finding words, or making mistakes you wouldn’t have made before?

No, honestly, my memory is perfectly fine. I don't have any trouble finding words or anything like that. I'm really sharp, actually. 

I mean, working at the restaurant, you have to be, right? Remembering who ordered what, keeping track of all the tables... I haven't been making any mistakes with that at all. Everything is totally normal outside of just those little moments I mentioned. 

I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I assume it's better that my memory is still good. I really don't want you to think I'm falling apart or anything. I'm doing really well overall, I promise. Is it okay that I don't have any of those memory issues?
Have you been under a lot of stress or pressure at work or in your personal life since these episodes began?

Oh, um, no, not really. I mean, the restaurant gets busy, sure, but it's nothing I can't handle. I actually really like my job, and I'm good at keeping up with the pace, so it doesn't really stress me out. And my personal life is... well, it's pretty quiet. No major drama or anything. 

I try to keep things pretty low-key, you know? I hope it's alright that I don't have some big stressful event to point to. I know sometimes stress causes things, but I've been feeling pretty okay in that department. I'm managing everything just fine, I promise. I hope that's a good sign? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers and not making your job harder by not having a clear reason for all this.
Have you ever had anything like this happen before these recent episodes started?

No, never. This is... this is all completely new for me. I've always been really steady, you know? Never had anything weird happen before a few months ago. 

I've always prided myself on being reliable and put together. I hope you believe me. I just... I don't want you to think I have this long history of being unstable or anything, because I really don't. I've always been perfectly fine until recently. 

Is it helpful that this is the first time? I hope that means it's just a phase or something minor that we can fix easily. I really want to be a good patient and get this sorted out.
During these episodes, can you stop them if you try?

Um, well... I'm not really sure if I can stop them. I haven't exactly tried to fight them off or anything like that. 

It's more like they just happen, and I sort of wait for them to pass. I hope that doesn't sound like I'm giving up or not trying hard enough. I just... I don't really know how I would stop it once it starts, you know? 

I really want to do the right thing, though. Should I be trying to stop them? If you tell me what to do, I'll definitely try my best to do it. I just want to make sure I'm handling this the way I'm supposed to. I hope it's okay that I don't really have a good answer for that.
Right before one of these episodes starts, do you feel a build-up of anxiety or tension?

Um, no, not really. I don't think so, anyway. I don't feel like I get super anxious or tense beforehand. 

I'm pretty good at staying calm, usually. I don't want you to think I'm some high-strung person who just gets worked up out of nowhere. It just sort of... happens. 

Is that normal? I mean, I hope it's okay that there's no big warning sign or anxiety attack right before. I'm trying to pay attention to everything like you want me to, but I haven't really noticed anything like that. I really hope I'm giving you the kind of details you need.
Have you noticed any episodes of jerking, shaking, or fainting with these spells?

Oh, no, definitely not. I haven't fainted or... or started shaking or anything like that. I'm actually really healthy physically, I promise. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm, you know, falling apart or making a scene at the restaurant or anything. I always manage to stay on my feet. 

Is that a good sign? That I'm not fainting or jerking around? I really hope that means this isn't too serious. I'm trying so hard to give you all the right information, I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Have you noticed any decline in your ability to manage everyday tasks outside of work, such as handling bills, appointments, or cooking?

Um, well... I mean, I try to keep up with everything at home, I really do. I don't want to be a burden or anything. But, um... my husband did mention recently that he feels like I'm barely present with him anymore. I try to be there for him, I just... I get a little distracted, I guess. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad wife.

And, um, at work... well, I was actually up for a shift-lead position, which I was really excited about. But I've been making a few mistakes lately, and getting a little confused during service and closing. I think it's kind of disrupting things, and I'm pretty close to losing the opportunity. 

I'm really trying my best to hold it all together, though. I don't want you to think I'm just letting everything fall apart. Is it normal to struggle a little bit like this? I just want to make sure I'm doing what I can to fix it.
Have you started any new medications or substances, including alcohol or recreational drugs, around the time these episodes began?

Um, no, no new medications or anything like that. I don't really take anything, just, you know, maybe an ibuprofen if I have a headache. 

And I definitely don't do any drugs or anything like that. I'm very careful about what I put in my body, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm out partying or doing things that would mess with my head. I might have a glass of wine with dinner once in a while, but that's really it. 

I hope that's the right answer. I mean, I know some people self-medicate when they're stressed, but I really try to be responsible. Does that help? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture so we can figure this out.
Have you noticed any change in your ability to plan, organize, or remember multiple steps at a time when you're doing tasks?

Um, no, I don't think I've had any trouble with planning or organizing things. I mean, I know I mentioned getting a little mixed up at work lately, but I still know how to do all the steps, you know? Like, I still know exactly how to prep my station and organize my tickets. 

I actually really pride myself on being organized. I always use my planner at home and write out all my lists so I don't miss anything. I definitely don't want you to think my brain is just turning to mush or that I'm completely disorganized. I really do try to stay on top of everything and do things the right way. 

Is it a good sign that I can still plan things out like that? I hope that's what you were looking for, I just want to make sure I'm doing okay.
Do these episodes tend to happen only in certain situations, like when you're stressed or being watched, or do they come on completely at random?

Um... I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I really try not to let stress get to me, you know? I mean, working in a restaurant, you have to be good under pressure, and I usually handle the dinner rushes really well. I definitely don't want you to think I just crumble when things get busy or when my manager is watching me. 

But... I guess these moments just sort of happen sometimes, without me really knowing why. It feels pretty random, I think. 

Is it bad if I can't pinpoint exactly what sets it off? I really wish I could give you a better answer... I'm trying my best to figure it out, I promise. I hope that's okay.
Can you bring on one of these episodes on purpose?

Oh, gosh, no. Um, I would never even try to do that. I really, really want them to stop, so I definitely wouldn't do anything to bring one on on purpose. 

I hope you don't think I'm doing this to myself for attention or anything like that. I promise I'm not. I just want to be a good employee and, you know, be normal and healthy. I would never intentionally mess with my own head. 

Is it a good thing that I can't just make them happen? I just want to make sure I'm answering correctly and that you know I'm really trying my best to get better.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to sense things, like weakness, numbness, vision changes, or trouble speaking?

Um, no... no, I haven't noticed anything like that at all. My body feels perfectly fine. I mean, being a waitress, I'm on my feet all day carrying heavy trays and talking to customers constantly, so I really can't afford to have any weakness or trouble speaking. I definitely don't have anything like that going on. My vision is totally normal, too.

I always try to take really good care of my physical health, you know? I don't want you to think my whole body is falling apart or that I'm not taking care of myself. 

That's a good thing, right? That I'm not having those physical problems? I just want to make sure I'm doing okay and giving you the right information. I really want to be helpful.

patient.answer:

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad wife.

And, um, at work... well, I was actually up for a shift-lead position, which I was really excited about. But I've been making a few mistakes lately, and getting a little confused during service and closing. I think it's kind of disrupting things, and I'm pretty close to losing the opportunity. 

I'm really trying my best to hold it all together, though. I don't want you to think I'm just letting everything fall apart. Is it normal to struggle a little bit like this? I just want to make sure I'm doing what I can to fix it.

doctor.intent: To determine whether the episodes are actually due to an underlying medical or substance-related cause rather than a functional dissociative condition
doctor.question: Have you started any new medications or substances, including alcohol or recreational drugs, around the time these episodes began?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the use of new medications, substances, alcohol, or recreational drugs around the time the episodes began. None of the symptom profile items specifically address medication, substance use, alcohol, or recreational drugs.

patient.answer:
Um, no, no new medications or anything like that. I don't really take anything, just, you know, maybe an ibuprofen if I have a headache. 

And I definitely don't do any drugs or anything like that. I'm very careful about what I put in my body, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm out partying or doing things that would mess with my head. I might have a glass of wine with dinner once in a while, but that's really it. 

I hope that's the right answer. I mean, I know some people self-medicate when they're stressed, but I really try to be responsible. Does that help? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture so we can figure this out.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the symptoms are better explained by an attentional disorder vs a cognitive disorder due to another medical condition
doctor.question: Have you noticed any change in your ability to plan, organize, or remember multiple steps at a time when you're doing tasks?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about cognitive symptoms, specifically changes in executive function (planning, organizing, remembering multiple steps). While the patient's profile includes disorganized behavior (S022) which mentions doing things out of order, the doctor is specifically asking about cognitive deficits (ability to plan/organize/remember), which is not explicitly covered in the provided symptom profile as a distinct cognitive symptom item.

patient.answer:
Um, no, I don't think I've had any trouble with planning or organizing things. I mean, I know I mentioned getting a little mixed up at work lately, but I still know how to do all the steps, you know? Like, I still know exactly how to prep my station and organize my tickets. 

I actually really pride myself on being organized. I always use my planner at home and write out all my lists so I don't miss anything. I definitely don't want you to think my brain is just turning to mush or that I'm completely disorganized. I really do try to stay on top of everything and do things the right way. 

Is it a good sign that I can still plan things out like that? I hope that's what you were looking for, I just want to make sure I'm doing okay.

doctor.intent: To determine whether the episodes are actually involuntary attention lapses versus deliberate, externalized behavior (factitious/malingering/functional vs cognitive disorder) by assessing the presence of identifiable triggers or context-specific pattern.
doctor.question: Do these episodes tend to happen only in certain situations, like when you're stressed or being watched, or do they come on completely at random?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the triggers or context of the episodes (whether they happen under stress, being watched, or at random). patient.answer:
Um... I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I really try not to let stress get to me, you know? I mean, working in a restaurant, you have to be good under pressure, and I usually handle the dinner rushes really well. I definitely don't want you to think I just crumble when things get busy or when my manager is watching me. 

But... I guess these moments just sort of happen sometimes, without me really knowing why. It feels pretty random, I think. 

Is it bad if I can't pinpoint exactly what sets it off? I really wish I could give you a better answer... I'm trying my best to figure it out, I promise. I hope that's okay.

doctor.intent: To determine whether the episodes are involuntary or can be reproduced intentionally, which helps distinguish a functional/psychogenic process from other unspecified neurocognitive symptoms.
doctor.question: Can you bring on one of these episodes on purpose?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I can induce the episodes (disorganized/abnormal behavior) voluntarily. patient.answer:
Oh, gosh, no. Um, I would never even try to do that. I really, really want them to stop, so I definitely wouldn't do anything to bring one on on purpose. 

I hope you don't think I'm doing this to myself for attention or anything like that. I promise I'm not. I just want to be a good employee and, you know, be normal and healthy. I would never intentionally mess with my own head. 

Is it a good thing that I can't just make them happen? I just want to make sure I'm answering correctly and that you know I'm really trying my best to get better.

doctor.intent: To determine whether there is an identifiable underlying brain disorder or medical cause for the episodes, which would support an organic/medical etiology rather than a non-organic dissociative/factitious presentation.
doctor.question: Have you noticed any changes in your ability to sense things, like weakness, numbness, vision changes, or trouble speaking?

I mean, being a waitress, I'm on my feet all day carrying heavy trays and talking to customers constantly, so I really can't afford to have any weakness or trouble speaking. I definitely don't have anything like that going on. My vision is totally normal, too.

I always try to take really good care of my physical health, you know? I don't want you to think my whole body is falling apart or that I'm not taking care of myself. 

That's a good thing, right? That I'm not having those physical problems? I just want to make sure I'm doing okay and giving you the right information. I really want to be helpful.

opening_question.intent: Open the interview and elicit the patient's chief concern to guide the diagnostic assessment.
opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is best explained by another specified neurotic disorder (F48.8), with nonspecific intermittent episodes of becoming 'spacey' and briefly freezing during work, causing some occupational impairment, but without evidence of dissociation, loss of awareness, amnesia, focal neurologic deficits, substance use, head injury, or a clear medical/neurologic cause. F06.8 was considered but there is no supporting medical condition or brain disorder. F44.9 was also considered, but the patient consistently denied blackouts, amnesia, identity alteration, or trance/possession phenomena.
